🚨🇲🇽 <u>EX-DEA CHIEF TELLS MEXICO TO INVITE US TROOPS IN</u>

Derek Maltz, former acting head of the DEA, publicly called on Mexico to join Washington's hemispheric "anti-cartel coalition" and to request US military forces on its own soil. It lands as the Trump administration pushes Latin America to accept joint operations inside its borders — the exact thing Sheinbaum has refused, again and again, under one principle: coordination without subordination.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>DUTCH TRADER VITOL BRIBED A PEMEX DIRECTOR — $400K, PEÑA NIETO ERA</u>

Contralínea puts a name to the Vitol bribery scheme: Luis Rafael Montanaro Sánchez, head of Pemex Etileno from 2016 to 2018, negotiating "agreements" over WhatsApp with Vitol's representative on trips to Houston. Vitol admitted in US court to roughly $400,000 in bribes to Mexican officials — part of a $10 million Latin American scheme — and paid Washington $163 million. It offered Mexico $30 million; Mexico won't take it until every official is named.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>CNI REPORT: DEA KIDNAPPED "EL MAYO" ON MEXICAN SOIL</u>

A CNI intelligence report confirms what Washington denied for a year: Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada was seized on Mexican territory. At the moment of his capture he phoned family to say DEA agents had detained him "as a result of a pact." Ex-ambassador Ken Salazar swore in August 2024 that no US agents took part — the FGR now calls that "completely false."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>WASHINGTON ASKS ITS MEXICO EMBASSY FOR LISTS OF "RADICAL LEFT" GROUPS</u>

Washington has ordered its embassy in Mexico — one of more than 20 — to compile files on "radical-left extremist" groups, ahead of Marco Rubio's July 15 summit gathering 60 governments against what Trump brands "transnational far-left terrorism." The country that ran Fast and Furious and armed Calderón's war now wants dossiers on Mexico's social movements.
📸 Vivienda para el Bienestar — Gómez Palacio, Durango · 11 de julio de 2026

🇲🇽✊ 5.1 million families have had their Infonavit mortgage debts cut or wiped out entirely. "5.1 million families — not loans, families — who have seen their debts either reduced or flat-out cancelled." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Gómez Palacio, Durango Under the reformed Infonavit, families who paid many times over their original loan are having debts forgiven. The institute now builds and delivers homes directly instead of financing banks and developers.

🇲🇽✊ 1.8 million new homes. Minimum 60 m². 11.5 million families with a guaranteed right to housing. "Before, they built 40-square-meter houses, far from where people worked or where there were schools and hospitals — some handed over with no running water, no drainage, no electricity. Many weren't even livable." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Gómez Palacio, Durango Vivienda para el Bienestar builds homes of at least 60 m² with full services, near jobs and schools — reversing the model that treated housing as disposable.

🇲🇽✊ "There are governments that take away, and governments that give. We are a government that gives to the people." President Sheinbaum handed housing keys directly to families in Gómez Palacio, Durango. — Claudia Sheinbaum, Vivienda para el Bienestar, Durango At the July 11 housing delivery, she drew the line between decades of neoliberal cutbacks and a program that treats a home as a right, not a product.

🇲🇽🔥🐉 Washington won't renew T-MEC for 16 years — Mexico isn't blinking

On July 1 the US declined to extend the T-MEC for another 16 years, downgrading it to annual reviews until it expires in 2036 — turning the "review" into a leash. Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard's answer: the treaty stays fully in force, 85% of Mexican exports already cross into the US tariff-free, and Mexico's own demand is to cut the Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminum and autos.

The empire preaches "free trade," then converts a trade deal into an annual loyalty test aimed squarely at China — which isn't even at the table. Mexico's reply is arithmetic: a record $23.6 billion in foreign investment in Q1 2026. A country multiplying its partners doesn't beg for renewal — it negotiates from strength.

🐉🇲🇽🌐 Chinese trains are already running in Mexico's cities — while Washington demands Mexico slam the door

On July 2 in Mexico City, China and Mexico held the "Green Future" forum. CRRC — the world's largest train manufacturer — signed a heritage-conservation deal with the National Museum of History at Chapultepec Castle, and laid out the CRRC-built light rail and electric transport now modernizing Mexico City and Guadalajara, complete with local workforce training and digital maintenance.

The timing is the whole point. As the T-MEC review opens and Washington pressures Mexico to treat China as contraband, Chinese rolling stock is already carrying Mexicans to work. Sovereignty isn't loyalty to one master — it's the freedom to build with everyone. Diversification is leverage.
